intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that annular epidermolytic ichthyosis-1 (AEI1) is caused by dominant mutation in the keratin-1 gene (KRT1; 139350) on chromosome 12q13.13.

checks.claim: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis-1 (AEI1) is caused by dominant mutation in the keratin-1 gene (KRT1).
checks.evidence_quote: is the result of dominant mutations in the keratin 1 and keratin 10 genes.
checks.explanation: The paper says AEI results from dominant mutations in both KRT1 and KRT10. It does not specify KRT1 for the AEI1 subtype.

checks.claim: The KRT1 gene is located on chromosome 12q13.13.
checks.evidence_quote: is the result of dominant mutations in the keratin 1 and keratin 10 genes.
checks.explanation: The paper does not give the chromosomal location. Under the stated rules, a gene's location is standard nomenclature added to a gene the paper names (keratin 1), so it counts as supported.

paragraphs.text: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is a rare phenotypic variant of epidermolytic ichthyosis, also known as congenital bullous ichthyosiform erythroderma (Mikilita et al., 2020). Blistering lesions may appear in infancy (Sahn et al., 1992). Affected individuals have recurrent outbreaks of annular, polycyclic, erythematous, scaly plaques on the trunk and proximal extremities, and some also have palmoplantar keratoderma (Mikilita et al., 2020). The plaques enlarge slowly and then resolve, and on histopathologic examination they show epidermolytic hyperkeratosis (Sahn et al., 1992).

paragraphs.text: Sahn et al. (1992) described a kindred that they suggested might represent a new phenotype of epidermolytic ichthyosis. The proband developed bullous and ichthyosiform skin lesions at the age of 8 months. At the age of 27 years, she developed numerous annular and polycyclic, erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques on the trunk and extremities, which enlarged slowly and then resolved. Histopathologic examination of these annular plaques revealed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.

paragraphs.text: Mikilita et al. (2020) listed one family with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis reported by Sybert et al. (1999), in which affected individuals had intermittent erythematous plaques. Palmoplantar involvement was reported in some of these individuals.

checks.evidence_quote: Sybert et al., 1999 | 10 | 5years/M
checks.explanation: Table 1 lists cases 10–12 from Sybert et al. (1999): a boy, his mother and his aunt, all from one family.

checks.explanation: Case 10 likewise had intermittent erythematous plaques.

checks.explanation: Cases 10 and 11 had palmoplantar involvement. No details are given for case 12.

paragraphs.text: Mikilita et al. (2020) noted that annular epidermolytic ichthyosis results from dominant mutations in keratin genes, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: Mikilita et al. (2020) noted that annular epidermolytic ichthyosis results from dominant mutations in keratin genes.
checks.evidence_quote: is the result of dominant mutations in the keratin 1 and keratin 10 genes.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis shows autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by extensive erythroderma and formation of blisters in early life
checks.explanation: The paper calls EI autosomal dominant and says AEI comes from dominant mutations. The reported families show parent-to-child transmission.

paragraphs.text: Joh et al. (1997) reported a mutation in the keratin-10 gene (KRT10) in annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.

checks.claim: Joh et al. (1997) reported a mutation in the keratin-10 gene (KRT10) in annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Molecular analysis revealed a novel tandem CG to GA 2-bp mutation in the same allele of keratin 10 in affected individuals, resulting in an arginine to glutamate substitution at residue 83 (R83E) of the 2B helical segment.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a KRT10 mutation in a family with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.
